chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding His saying, Exalted and Blessed is He: 'So there is no hostility except against the oppressors.' He said: 'The children of the killers of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'
My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, similarly.

key_terms.أَوْلَادُ قَتَلَةِ الْحُسَيْنِ: The children of the killers of al-Husayn
key_terms.فَلا عُدْوانَ إِلَّا عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ: So there is no hostility except against the oppressors (Quran 2:193)

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'oppressors' referred to in the verse 'Fa la 'udwana illa 'ala al-zalimin' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) offers a specific exegetical link between the Quranic command to fight only the oppressors (2:193) and the lineage of the killers of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.). This interpretation underscores the theological justification for avenging the blood of the Ahl al-Bayt, framing the descendants of the Karbala martyrs' enemies as the primary 'oppressors' in this context. It highlights the enduring spiritual and political significance of Karbala within Shia jurisprudence and theology.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 6. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Isā, from Samā’ah ibn Mihrān, who said:
Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said, “The verse, ‘There should be no hostility except against the oppressors’ [2:193] refers to the children of the killers of Ḥusain (a.s.).”

The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chain: My father, from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, and from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Isā, from Samā’ah ibn Mihrān, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (a.s.).
